les: Wat ons van ons voorouers erf
kaps_punt: Wat is erfenis - 2 uur; en: Erfenis in voorwerpe: Voorbeeld: Goue voorwerpe by Mapungubwe: Limpopo

items.bewering: Erfenis is dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'About World Heritage' (whc.unesco.org/en/about/heritage): 'Heritage is our legacy from the past, what we live with today, and what we pass on to future generations.' The lesson's definition maps onto all three parts (receive from the past, keep, pass on).

items.bewering: Ons ryk erfenis kom uit baie kulture en behoort aan almal in ons land.
items.bron: South African government Heritage Month and Heritage Day material: gov.za 2026 Heritage Month key messages ('celebrate the diverse cultures, languages, traditions and histories that make South Africa unique'); The Presidency ('the rich cultural tapestry that makes up our nation'); SAnews, 'Heritage Day celebrates SA's rich tapestry of cultures'. This is a statement of national heritage policy, and it matches how the state frames it.

items.bewering: Erfenis is tasbaar as jy dit kan sien en aanraak. Dit kan 'n plek, gebou of voorwerp wees.
items.bron: UNESCO's split between tangible heritage (monuments, groups of buildings, sites under the 1972 World Heritage Convention, plus movable objects) and intangible heritage (2003 Convention, ich.unesco.org). Places, buildings and objects are the standard tangible examples.

items.bewering: Musiek, feeste en jou gesin se stories is nie-tasbaar. Jy kan dit nie aanraak nie.
items.bron: UNESCO 2003 Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, five domains (ich.unesco.org/en/intangible-cultural-heritage-00052): oral traditions and expressions (family stories), performing arts (music), and social practices, rituals and festive events (festivals). One simplification is acceptable at this level: the Convention also counts the instruments and objects linked to a practice as part of it. A drum can be touched, but the music cannot, and the lesson's sentence is about the music.

items.bewering: Plekke wat vir die hele mensdom waardevol is, word deur UNESCO as wêrelderfenisterreine erken.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Convention (1972) and whc.unesco.org: sites of 'outstanding universal value' to humanity are inscribed on the World Heritage List. The formal decision is made by the World Heritage Committee, which is part of UNESCO, so 'deur UNESCO erken' is fair.

items.bewering: So 'n plek moet vir toekomstige geslagte bewaar word.
items.bron: UNESCO, 'The World Heritage Convention' (whc.unesco.org/en/convention/): States Parties commit to protecting and preserving the heritage on their territory for future generations. The Convention's text also names the duty to transmit it to future generations.

items.bewering: Suid-Afrika het 12 van hierdie plekke.
items.bron: Twelve sites as of 13 November 2026. (1) SAnews (government news agency, 29 July 2024): the two serial properties inscribed in 2024, the Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites and the Pleistocene Occupation Sites, 'will bring South Africa's number of World Heritage sites to 12'. (2) Wikipedia, 'List of World Heritage Sites in South Africa' (edited November 2026): 12 sites, 7 cultural, 4 natural and 1 mixed. It records only a 2025 extension of iSimangaliso into Mozambique's Maputo National Park, which changed no count, and no 2026 change. (3) The 48th World Heritage Committee session (Busan, July 2026) inscribed 25 new sites, and none is South African. Checked in UNESCO's news item of 28 July 2026 (whc.unesco.org/en/news/2915) and Outlook Traveller's list of all 25. Caveat: UNESCO's own state-party page for South Africa returned HTTP 403 and could not be read directly. This number will go stale at the next new inscription, so re-check it at every reprint.

items.bewering: Die Victoria-waterval in Zambië en Zimbabwe is natuurlik, want dit word vir die natuur self erken.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Mosi-oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls': a World Heritage Site inscribed in 1989 on natural criteria (vii) and (viii) only, and shared by Zambia and Zimbabwe. The place is right and the classification is right. The lesson names the countries, so a learner will not count it among South Africa's 12 from the sentence above it.

items.bewering: Mapungubwe in Limpopo is kultureel, want mense het daar gewoon en gebou.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'List of World Heritage Sites in South Africa': Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape, Cultural, 2003, criteria (ii)(iii)(iv)(v). Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe': Mapungubwe National Park, Limpopo. The reason given matches what the listing recognises, the remains of the kingdom's palace and settlement areas. It also fits the 1972 Convention's definition of cultural heritage as 'works of man'.

items.bewering: Robbeneiland is ook kultureel, want dit laat ons dink aan belangrike mense en aan wat daar gebeur het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Robben Island' (WHS box): Cultural, 1999, criteria (iii) and (vi). Criterion (vi) covers association with events and ideas of outstanding significance, here political imprisonment from 1961 to 1996, including Nelson Mandela, and the island as a symbol. The paraphrase 'belangrike mense en wat daar gebeur het' is a fair simplification.

items.bewering: Die Maloti-Drakensbergpark is gemeng, want dit het albei: mooi berge en ou rotskuns van die San.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Maloti-Drakensberg Park': mixed (cultural and natural), criteria (i)(iii)(vii)(x), shared by South Africa and Lesotho. UNESCO's listing text, quoted by several sources (IUCN World Heritage Outlook, Smarthistory): 'spectacular natural landscape' and 'wealth of rock paintings made by the San people over a period of 4000 years'. 'Mooi berge' corresponds to criterion (vii), natural beauty, and the San rock art to (i) and (iii). One UNESCO document notes that some 19th- and 20th-century paintings are attributed to Bantu-speaking people. That does not make the lesson's 'ou rotskuns van die San' false, because the old art is San.

items.bewering: Parallel set tested as a set: Victoria Falls = natural (recognised for nature), Mapungubwe = cultural (people lived and built), Robben Island = cultural (people and events), Maloti-Drakensberg = mixed (both).
items.bron: Every classification agrees with the UNESCO inscription type: Victoria Falls is natural, Mapungubwe and Robben Island are cultural, and Maloti-Drakensberg is mixed (sources above). I also tested the four reasons as a rule a learner might reason further with. The rule would be: cultural = people's works and history; natural = the nature itself; mixed = both. It sorts all four examples correctly and contradicts none of them. One risk was checked and is not present. A learner might read 'mense het daar gewoon' as 'any place people lived is cultural', and the San lived in the Drakensberg. But the lesson calls the Drakensberg mixed because of the San's rock art, which is consistent with that reading, not against it. No item in the set is a contested classification. The sorting is UNESCO's own, not a teaching convention.

items.bewering: Sowat 800 jaar gelede het mense van die Mapungubwe-koninkryk voorwerpe van goud gemaak.
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe': made during the Kingdom of Mapungubwe (1220-1300). Google Arts & Culture and the University of Pretoria collection description date the rhino from the 'original gold grave' to about CE 1250-1290. Britannica Kids and The Heritage Portal both say about '800 years ago'. SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': a gold and ivory trading centre from about 1200 to 1300 and evidence of early gold smelting, so the objects were made there. 1220-1290 is about 730-800 years ago, and 'sowat 800' is an acceptable rounding with 'sowat' in front. Note: the rhino itself is closer to 750 years old. Write '800 jaar' without 'sowat' and it becomes too precise.

items.bewering: Die goud is op die heuwel gevind waar die koning gewoon het.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': gold and iron artefacts were recovered on Mapungubwe Hill in 1932, and royalty and the nobility built on the high ground. Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe': found in a royal grave on Mapungubwe Hill, with the ruling elite living separately on the hilltop. World History Encyclopedia, 'Mapungubwe': the king and his court lived in stone enclosures on the highest part of the hill and were buried at the top. It is archaeological interpretation that the hill was the king's residence, but it is the established reading across these sources.

items.bewering: Die bekendste stuk is 'n renoster van dun goudplaatjies om 'n houtvorm.
items.bron: Superlative 'bekendste': SAHO, 'Mapungubwe', calls the golden rhinoceros 'the best known' of the royal objects found there, and SANParks calls it the symbol of Mapungubwe. Construction: Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe', describes wood covered in thin sheets of gold. Popular Archaeology and the University of Pretoria material describe hollow gold foil over a wooden core that has since decayed, held on with tiny gold tacks. 'Dun goudplaatjies om 'n houtvorm' is correct. It makes no claim that the figure is solid gold, which is the usual popular error.

items.bewering: Al hierdie goud is tasbare erfenis.
items.bron: The objects are physical artefacts held in the University of Pretoria's Mapungubwe Collection (Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe'). Movable cultural objects are tangible heritage under UNESCO's tangible/intangible distinction (see above). This is consistent with the lesson's own definition of 'tasbaar'.

items.bewering: Dit is getuienis van knap vakmense en van leiers met groot mag.
items.bron: SAHO, 'Mapungubwe': a class-based society with royalty on the hill, evidence of early gold smelting, and one burial alone with a large quantity of gold. Wikipedia, 'Golden Rhinoceros of Mapungubwe': the first known class-based society in southern Africa, and the figure points to a wealthy trading centre. Gold grave goods in hilltop royal burials are the standard evidence for both skilled metalworkers and a powerful elite.

items.bewering: erfenis: Dinge en gewoontes wat ons uit die verlede ontvang, bewaar en aan die volgende geslagte oordra.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'About World Heritage': 'our legacy from the past ... what we pass on to future generations'. Word for word the same as the study block, so the two cannot drift apart.

items.bewering: tasbare erfenis: Erfenis wat jy kan sien en aanraak, soos plekke, geboue en voorwerpe.
items.bron: UNESCO 1972 Convention (monuments, groups of buildings, sites) and the general tangible/intangible distinction. True when read on its own; the examples follow 'soos', so the list does not claim to be complete.

items.bewering: nie-tasbare erfenis: Erfenis wat jy nie kan aanraak nie, soos musiek, feeste en tradisies.
items.bron: UNESCO 2003 Convention domains (ich.unesco.org): performing arts (music), social practices, rituals and festive events (festivals), and oral and other traditions. True when read on its own.

items.bewering: UNESCO: Die Verenigde Nasies se Organisasie vir Onderwys, Wetenskap en Kultuur, wat wêrelderfenisterreine erken.
items.bron: UNESCO = United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (whc.unesco.org/en/convention/; Wikipedia, 'World Heritage Convention'). The Afrikaans rendering is a correct translation of the name. The recognition is done through UNESCO's World Heritage Committee under the 1972 Convention.

items.bewering: wêrelderfenisterrein: 'n Plek wat UNESCO erken omdat dit vir die hele mensdom waardevol is.
items.bron: UNESCO World Heritage Convention: sites of 'outstanding universal value' are inscribed on the World Heritage List (whc.unesco.org/en/convention/). A fair simplification, and true when read on its own.

items.bewering: getuienis: Wat 'n bron vir ons wys oor wat in die verlede gebeur het.
items.bron: Historical-thinking usage: evidence is what a source (an object, document or photograph from the past) shows us, and we use it to support what we know about the past (historyskills.com, 'primary sources'; Wikipedia, 'Historical thinking'; National Archives of Australia, 'Research skills'). It fits the lesson's own use, where the gold objects are the source and what they show is 'getuienis'.

opsomming: Every claim holds, including the count of 12 South African World Heritage Sites (no South African site was added in July 2026, but re-check it at every reprint), the natural, cultural and mixed examples tested as a set, and the one superlative, the gold rhino as the best-known piece.
